key_insight: PQuantML is an open-source, hardware-aware toolkit that unifies pruning and fixed-point quantization into an end-to-end workflow, making it easy to train and deploy latency-efficient neural networks for constrained runtimes.
problem_solved: Addresses the fragmented, engineering-heavy process of producing compressed models that meet strict latency and hardware constraints by providing a single interface to apply and tune pruning and quantization, jointly or separately.
method: Unified API to apply pruning and fixed-point quantization within a single end-to-end training and deployment pipeline.
Implements multiple pruning algorithms across different granularities (e.g., layer-/channel-/weight-level) so compression can be tailored to model and hardware.
Hardware-aware fixed-point quantization with configurable bitwidths and quantization parameters, plus tooling to combine pruning + quantization for latency-aware model optimization.
impact: Reduces engineering overhead and speeds up the path from research to deployment for models targeting latency-sensitive hardware, enabling practitioners to meet efficiency targets more predictably and reproducibly.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data → training → pruning & quantization (joint or separate) → hardware-aware deployment
Trade-off chart: accuracy vs latency/size showing baseline, pruning-only, quantization-only, and combined results
Illustration of pruning granularities (global/structured/channel/weight) with simple network sketches
Icon set: toolbox/library (open-source), chip/latency meter (hardware-aware), gear (configurable quantization), scissors (pruning)
paper_title: PQuantML: A Tool for End-to-End Hardware-aware Model Compression
paper_authors: Roope Niemi, Anastasiia Petrovych, Arghya Ranjan Das, Enrico Lupi, Chang Sun
